entries.overview: A pair of slender muscular tubes about 25 to 30 cm long descending down the back abdominal wall to the pelvis.
entries.function: Propels urine smoothly downward from each kidney into the urinary bladder via rhythmic smooth-muscle waves.

facts: Enters the back wall of the bladder at an oblique angle so filling pressure seals the opening against backflow.
Moves urine actively by peristalsis rather than relying only on gravity.

entries.overview: A hollow, balloon-like muscular sac tucked cleanly behind the front pubic bones on the pelvic floor.
entries.function: Stores urine comfortably at low pressure until voluntary signals squeeze it empty through the urethra.

facts: Lined by stretchy transitional epithelium and inner folds that flatten out as volume increases.
Its smooth muscle wall (detrusor muscle) contracts during urination while sphincters relax.

entries.overview: A thin-walled fibromuscular canal leading from the bottom neck of the bladder to the outside of the body.
entries.function: Conducts stored urine out of the body during urination while internal and external sphincters regulate timing.

facts: Guarded by an involuntary smooth-muscle internal sphincter and a voluntary skeletal-muscle external sphincter.
Differs in length between sexes: shorter (~4 cm) in females and longer (~20 cm) in males.
